propositions: Four dispatch call sites use `cast()` to access optional capability members (`add_comment`, `set_relationship`) but perform no runtime check before the call, unlike `fetcher.py` which guards with `hasattr`

An `AttributeError` from a missing capability is swallowed by a broad `except Exception` handler, so the mutation silently fails and the pass reports success, conflating capability-absent (designed skip) with capability-present-but-failing (real error)

The reconciler is inconsistent with itself — two guarding patterns exist in the same codebase, and the unguarded sites are vulnerable when a second backend (DC) does not implement optional capabilities
The latent gap becomes a live defect when Data Center removes the assumption that all transports implement all capabilities
The four call sites must gate on `isinstance(client, SupportsCapability)` before calling optional members and log/alert distinctly when a capability is absent versus when it fails
Relocating `_call_with_retry` (~75 LOC) from `dispatch_one.py` to `dispatch_apply_phases.py` creates room for guards while respecting the 800-LOC module-size constraint
